We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We are building the most automated lab in the world, and that does not stop at the bench. A company that AI agents can run experiments in has to automate everything around the experiment too — procurement, hiring, admin, and finance. Finance is one of the most automatable functions in any company and almost nobody has actually done it. We intend to.

That is the job: build an AI-powered finance stack. Our ledger, billing, cards and payroll all expose APIs, and we already close the books against them programmatically rather than by hand. You would take that much further, to where the model, the close, the cash view and the margin analysis largely run themselves, and your week goes on the decisions instead of the reconciliation.

You would be our first finance hire, and it is hands-on. You will build the forecast, run the close across two entities, own cash, and be the person who can say what a protein actually costs us to make.

What You'll Do

- Own the forecast. Both directions: bottom-up from lab capacity, throughput and price per protein, and top-down P&L, burn and runway.

- Own gross margin. What does an experiment actually cost us — DNA, reagents, consumables, instrument time, labour? Which products and which customers lose us money?

- Own pricing, with commercial. What we charge, why, and where the floor is. Pricing at a lab company is a finance question wearing a sales hat.

- Own the close. Group consolidation and intercompany management. Make it fast, make it correct, make it boring.

- Own cash. Bank and card accounts across Switzerland and the US, AP runs, AR collection, payment timing. Know where the money is and where it is going before anyone asks.

- Keep us compliant. Tax, VAT, audit, payroll, and the external firms we work with. You are not a lawyer or an accountant, but you know when to call one.

- Investor reporting, fundraising support, and treasury management. 

- Equipment leasing and asset management. The lab runs on millions of francs of instruments. Lease or buy, how we finance it, what it does to the balance sheet, and keeping the asset register honest as we expand.

- Automate all of the above. 

What We're Looking For

- You have built a finance function, not just worked in one. Several years in finance at a startup that actually scaled, and ideally you were early enough to have set things up rather than inherited them.

- You can build a real model. Not a template. A model that ties operational reality — throughput, yield, capacity, headcount — to cash, and that survives someone pulling on it.

- You write code, or you are visibly about to. SQL at minimum, Python ideally. This is the hard requirement most finance candidates will fail, and we mean it. We run on Claude Code across the company, and every system finance touches has an API behind it. The best version of this person automates their own function, writes their own tooling, and finds leverage the rest of us have not thought of. If your instinct is that finance is a spreadsheet-and-portal job, we will frustrate each other.

- You understand the cost structure of a physical business. Reagents, instruments, consumables, capex versus COGS, yield loss. Lab, hardware, or manufacturing backgrounds all translate. Pure SaaS finance does not, on its own.

- Swiss and European finance experience. VAT, social charges, employment law. A US entity alongside a Swiss one is a plus.

- Ambitious, and in it for the company. We want someone who intends to be running finance at a much larger Adaptyv in three years, and who cares about what we are building rather than the title on the door.

- Trustworthy with everything. Salaries, revenue, investor communications, board material. All of it crosses your desk.

Scope

We are a small company and nobody here has clean edges around their job. You will end up in the lab, in a room with a customer, and every so often doing something that is nobody's job simply because it needs doing.

The centre of gravity is the numbers: the model, the close, cash, margin, pricing, and the board pack. That is the part that is yours and the part we will judge the role on. Procurement is a separate hire and the two of you will be joined at the hip on cost, but the sourcing and the vendor relationships are not yours to run.

One thing it is not: a bookkeeping seat. The mechanical layer is handled, and if that is the job you want, this one will bore you.

Why This Role Is Interesting

Most first-finance-hires at a startup spend three years cleaning up a SaaS P&L. Here, the finance question and the product question are the same question: an automated lab is a machine for converting money into experimental data, and how efficiently it does that is literally the business. You will be building the model of that machine, at a company that is about to expand it several-fold, while it is being used by the best pharma companies and the best AI labs in the world. And you will do it with a founding team that will hand you the API keys and get out of your way.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. About the Role

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.

What You'll Do

- Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

- Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

- Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

- Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

- Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

- Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

- Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

- Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science).

What We're Looking For

- MSc / PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics.

- Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you.

- Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

- Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand.

- You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling internally, and the people who get the most done here are the ones who reach for it by default: writing the analysis script, querying the database, building the one-off dashboard. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place.

- A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found.

- A fast learner. Our platform, our assays, and our software change constantly. You'll be handed unfamiliar tools and expected to be productive with them quickly.

- Startup speed, not academic pace. Experiments ship to paying customers on deadlines. Getting a good answer this week beats a perfect one next quarter, and we'd rather flag an ambiguous result than sit on it.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

This is not a lab technician position. This is a senior scientist who owns assay quality, data QC and controls, and production troubleshooting across the entire experimental pipeline.

The production team runs 150+ experiments per month across expression, BLI, SPR, thermostability, and enzyme activity. When something goes wrong (failed expression, anomalous binding data, instrument artifacts), this person diagnoses the root cause and fixes it. As the assay and instrumentation portfolio expands, this person translates new R&D methods into production-ready protocols, builds robust methods that junior technicians can execute reliably, and designs comprehensive controls that enable automated QC and data processing.

This is a player-coach position. You will still run experiments personally, especially as you integrate into the lab, but you will also elevate the whole team's capabilities.

What You'll Do

- Troubleshoot production failures across the full pipeline. A batch of proteins isn't expressing: is it the construct design, the expression system, or the media? BLI sensorgrams look noisy: is it the sensor tips, the sample prep, or an instrument issue? You figure it out, fix it, and make the cause easier to identify next time.

- Develop and document SOPs for new assays as the portfolio expands. Take methods from the R&D team and make them production-ready: robust, reproducible, and executable by junior technicians without hand-holding.

- Mentor a growing production team. Set quality standards, review data, train new hires, and build a culture where people flag problems early instead of hiding them.

- Work at the intersection of biology, automation, and QC. Collaborate with researchers, laboratory technicians, and automation engineers on protocol optimization for work cells, and with software on LabOS protocol integration.

- Own the relationship between assay science and throughput. The easy version of every assay doesn't scale, and the scalable version often sacrifices quality. You find the right tradeoff.

What We're Looking For

- Deep hands-on expertise in protein production: expression (E. coli, mammalian, cell-free), purification (IMAC, SEC), and biophysical characterization (BLI and SPR at minimum). This isn't negotiable. You need to have done this work yourself, at volume.

- PhD in protein biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3–5 years in a production or development role at a CRO, foundry, or high-throughput lab. Academic postdocs count if the work was high-throughput and production-oriented.

- Experience with high-throughput workflows. You're comfortable with 96-well plates and liquid handlers, not just single-column purifications. You've optimized protocols for scale, not just for one perfect result.

- Mentorship mindset. You've managed or trained junior scientists before. You enjoy teaching and get satisfaction from watching your team grow.

- Troubleshooting instinct. When data looks wrong, your first impulse is to understand why, not to rerun the experiment and hope it works.

- Quality-obsessed but pragmatic. You care deeply about data quality, but you also understand that production has deadlines and sometimes "good enough" is the right call.

- Bridge between R&D and production. You can speak both languages: the exploratory mindset of research and the reproducibility demands of production.

What You'll Do

- Control lab instruments — liquid handlers, robot arms, plate readers, incubators, analytical devices — programmatically in Python, ideally with PyLabRobot / PyHamilton, rather than locking workflows into proprietary software.

- Build and integrate work cells: get multiple instruments working together as one orchestrated unit that runs unattended.

- Bring new instruments online by reverse-engineering their control protocols and building drivers that expose them to the rest of the stack.

- Write the software glue — drivers, integrations, small services — that connects hardware to our platform (mostly Python, with some TypeScript).

- Partner with biologists to turn new assays into reliable automated workflows, then keep them running: diagnosing and fixing the mechanical, electrical, and software failures that come with 24/7 production.

- Push throughput and reliability up continuously — better error recovery, smarter scheduling, sturdier hardware.

What We're Looking For

- Maker and hacker attitude. You like taking systems apart, figuring out how they work, and building the thing that makes them work better. You'd rather script an instrument than click through it.

- Strong software engineering skills. You write real Python and can structure code others can maintain — drivers, integrations, services — not just throwaway scripts. You'll pick up TypeScript where needed.

- Lab automation experience. Hands-on with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling is a strong plus. Direct experience automating instruments and workflows matters more than the specific platform.

- Self-starter and independent. You see what needs building and build it. You don't wait for a spec, and you don't need a vendor training course to get going.

- AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

- Hardware comfort is a plus. Electronics, microcontrollers, 3D printing, CAD, or fabrication experience all help, but they're not required if your software and automation skills are strong.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

Our lab is a factory. DNA goes in, characterized proteins come out, and a customer gets results in days rather than the months a CRO would take. Everything that machine consumes — synthesized genes, reagents, consumables, biosensors, catalog proteins — is something we buy, on lead times we do not control. It is also most of what a protein costs to make, which makes procurement one of the biggest levers on gross margin in the business.

So far scientists have bought what they need, decisions get made in hours, and nothing blocks an experiment. That was the right trade while we were proving the thing works. But we are multiplying lab throughput several times over, and at that volume procurement becomes a discipline: real terms with the suppliers we already buy from heavily, qualified second sources where we currently have one, inventory that is planned rather than remembered. Nobody has taken that on yet.

You would be our first dedicated supply chain hire, and it is hands-on — you do the sourcing and the negotiating yourself. One thing makes it harder than a typical procurement job: our assay portfolio keeps expanding, and every new assay brings new reagents. You are not optimizing a static supply chain, you are building one that flexes with the science. How far the role goes from there is up to you.

What You'll Do

- Own procurement end to end. Every input to the lab, from gene synthesis down to gloves. Requests, POs, receiving, vendor onboarding, the lot.

- De-risk the supply chain. Too much of what we depend on has exactly one supplier. Find second sources, qualify them properly with the science team, and keep them warm, so that switching is a decision we make rather than an emergency we react to.

- Negotiate. Build the supplier relationships across our DNA, reagent, biosensor and catalog-protein vendors, put volume commitments and pricing agreements in place, and go get the margin back.

- Drive down the cost of a protein. Go category by category and take cost out of each. A few francs per protein, multiplied across the volumes we are heading toward, is a seven-figure line.

- Stay ahead of the science. When R&D says they are adding a new assay next quarter, you should already be sourcing the reagents for it.

- Set inventory policy, and make the numbers true. Reorder points and safety stock, so we never stall a customer experiment on a stockout and never have six figures of reagents quietly expiring in a freezer. You decide what should be on the shelves and how much of it.

- Plan supply for the lab expansion. Model what several-fold throughput actually needs — volumes, lead times, storage, cash tied up in stock — and have it in place before the capacity comes online, not after.

- Own landed cost. Shipping, customs, import duties, VAT recoverability, cold chain. We import a lot of biology into Switzerland and both the cost and the failure modes matter.

- Own COGS with Finance. Procurement and finance are the two halves of gross margin, and you are the procurement half.

- Automate the whole thing. Ordering, tracking, and reconciliation should mostly run themselves.

What We're Looking For

- You have worked in supply chain or procurement in a physical, technical business. Biotech, a CRO, or another life science company is ideal, and you understand reagent categories — enzymes, antibodies, media, resins, plasticware — and how they are actually sourced. Hardware manufacturing or another high-mix production setting translates well. Buying software licences does not. You do not need to have run a supply chain organization before; you do need to be ready to own one.

- You think in margins. Saving a few francs per protein across tens of thousands of proteins a month is a number that should make you sit up.

- You are technical enough to talk to scientists. You do not need a degree in biology, but you will be qualifying an alternative supplier for a reagent that a protein biochemist depends on, and you need to be able to have that conversation properly rather than forwarding it.

- You can negotiate. Comfortable sitting across from vendors who have been selling into labs for thirty years, and comfortable walking away.

- You automate. We run on Claude Code across the company and our lab system has an API. Some of our largest suppliers still require a human to upload a spreadsheet to a portal, and we consider that a bug rather than a fact of life. The best version of this person is writing scripts against our systems and our vendors' systems, not clicking through them. If your instinct is that procurement is a portal-and-email job, we will frustrate each other.

- Obsessive about the details that bite. Lead times, expiry dates, lot numbers, minimum order quantities. Nothing falls through.

- You want to grow fast. We are going from roughly 25 people to roughly 50 in the next year, and the lab spend grows faster than the headcount does.

- Swiss or EU import/export experience is a strong plus.

Scope

We are a small company and nobody here has clean edges around their job. You will end up in the lab, in a spreadsheet with Finance, on the phone with a courier, and every so often doing something that is nobody's job simply because it needs doing. That is the deal, and if it sounds unappealing then we are probably not the right place.

What we do want to be clear about is where the centre of gravity is. This role is about what we buy, who we buy it from, what we pay, and how reliably it turns up. Sourcing, negotiation, supplier relationships, inventory, resilience, cost. Plenty of other things will land on your desk and you should take them, but that is the part that is yours and the part we will judge the role on.

One thing it is not: an order-taking job. You are not a mailbox between scientists and vendors. You decide what we source and from whom, and we expect you to argue with us about it.

Why This Role Is Interesting

Most supply chain jobs are about keeping a stable system stable. This one is about building the supply chain for a lab that is about to grow several-fold, at a company where the cost and reliability of an experiment more or less is the product. Every franc you take out of the cost of a protein, and every week you take out of a lead time, shows up directly in what we can offer customers and in whether AI-designed biology is cheap enough to be worth doing at scale. There are not many procurement jobs where the leverage is that direct, or that visible to the people running the company.

We are going from roughly 25 people to roughly 50 in the next twelve months. This is the hire that fixes it, and we want to aim high with it. Not a recruiter who works a req list. Someone who owns talent as a function: what we hire for, how we assess it, how we pitch it, who does the recruiting, and what the org actually looks like on the other side of doubling.

The hard part of this job is that our roles don't sit in one talent pool. In the same week you might be trying to find a protein biochemist who can read a sensorgram, an engineer who can make a liquid handler behave, and a backend engineer who has never touched biology. Those people read different signals, hang out in different places, and are sold with different pitches. You have to be able to hold all of that at once, and know which one you're talking to.

We would love someone who can speak both languages well enough to spot exceptional people themselves. You don't need a PhD and you don't need to ship code. You do need enough real understanding of what our scientists and engineers actually do that you can tell the difference between someone who sounds impressive and someone who is.

This is a Lausanne role. Most of the company is here, most of the people you'll hire will be here, and the job is much easier when you can walk over to a hiring manager and argue about a candidate in person.

What You'll Do

- Own hiring end to end. Define what we're hiring for with the team, write and post the roles, build the pipeline, run the process, and close people.

- Build the recruiting team. As we scale, you'll hire and manage specialist recruiters, most likely a technical recruiter first. You'll be a player-coach for a long time before you're purely a manager.

- Own the inbound pipeline. We get a lot of applicants and a real share of them are strong. Right now good people can get lost in the pile. Making that never happen is one of the most valuable things you can do here.

- Run our work trials. A lot of our best hires come through paid work trials rather than interview loops. Scheduling them, matching them to the right people internally, and making them a great experience for the candidate is core to the job.

- Make the pitch. You'll often be the first human a candidate talks to. You're selling the mission, and you should genuinely believe it.

- Own Ashby and push it further. Our ATS is already wired into AI tooling: automated candidate scoring, assisted review, templated and scheduled candidate comms. You'll inherit that and be expected to make it better, not merely operate it.

- Work with hiring managers across biology, software, automation, and commercial. Different teams, different bars, different definitions of good. You'll help each of them get sharper about what they actually need.

- Build the parts of the org that hiring touches: leveling, compensation bands, interview structure, onboarding, and how we make offers. Fast and light, not corporate.

What We're Looking For

- You've hired technical people at real depth, for several years, in a high-growth environment. You've owned searches that mattered and closed people who had other options.

- You can talk to scientists and to engineers. You understand enough biology and enough software or lab automation to run a credible conversation, ask a sharp follow-up, and form your own view of someone's quality. This is the thing we care most about and the thing most recruiters cannot do.

- You are not a mercenary. We are not looking for someone optimizing for placements or fee cycles. We want someone who cares about what we're building, who wants the company to be excellent in ten years, and who treats every hire as a long-term bet rather than a filled seat.

- You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling across the company, including in hiring. The best version of this person is automating their own pipeline, writing their own scripts against Ashby, and finding leverage the rest of us haven't thought of. If your instinct is that recruiting is purely a human craft that shouldn't be automated, we'll frustrate each other.

- Self-starter, high autonomy. Nobody will hand you a prioritized req list. You'll figure out what's most broken, fix it, and tell us what you did.

- Fast learner. You'll be dropped into unfamiliar technical domains constantly and expected to get to a useful level of understanding quickly.

- Startup speed, not corporate process. Good candidates disappear in days. We'd rather move fast and occasionally be wrong than run a beautiful process that loses people.

- Good taste in people, and the confidence to hold a bar. Part of this job is telling a founder that the person they liked isn't good enough.

- Bonus: experience with the Swiss labor market, hiring in European biotech or deep tech, or building a talent function from nothing.

What This Role Is Not

- Not a coordinator role. You'll do scheduling when it needs doing, but if that's what you want to do all day, this will bore you.

- Not a pure people or HR generalist role. Payroll, benefits, and Swiss employment admin exist and are mostly handled. Talent is the job.

- Not an agency-style seat. You're not filling reqs handed down to you. You're deciding, with the founders, what we should be hiring for at all.

Why This Role Is Interesting

Most talent leaders inherit a hiring machine and tune it. You'd be building one, at a company that is unusual enough to be genuinely fun to pitch: an automated lab that AI agents can run experiments in, used by the best pharma companies and the best AI labs in the world. The people you hire over the next two years will decide whether that works. There are not many jobs where the leverage is that direct.

title: Synthesis Instrumentation Engineer
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on scientist-engineer to help build our next-generation DNA synthesis platform, enabling high-throughput, cost-effective production of large and diverse DNA libraries. You'll work at the intersection of chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, and hardware development, designing and building prototypes, running experiments, and optimizing processes to turn new synthesis technologies into reliable, scalable production systems.

DNA synthesis is a fundamental part of our protein engineering platform. We're developing new approaches to dramatically increase synthesis throughput while reducing cost and turnaround time.

You'll work closely with our scientific and engineering teams to develop and prototype new DNA synthesis technologies. Your focus will be on translating scientific concepts into working hardware and experimental systems, designing and building prototypes, testing different approaches, and continuously improving their performance.

This is a highly hands-on, interdisciplinary role combining experimental science with practical engineering. You'll take ownership of prototype development, experimental validation, and process optimization, helping move promising technologies from early concepts to reliable, scalable systems.

We're looking for someone who enjoys building things, solving technical problems, and working across disciplines. You don't need to be an expert in DNA synthesis, but you should have strong scientific fundamentals, an engineering mindset, and experience turning ideas into working prototypes.

What You'll Do

- Design, build, and test prototypes for next-generation DNA synthesis technologies.

- Translate scientific and technical requirements into practical engineering designs and experimental setups.

- Scope and evaluate different technical approaches, components, materials, and equipment for prototype development.

- Develop and optimize the chemistry, materials, and processes underlying the synthesis platform.

- Design and execute experiments to characterize performance, identify limitations, and improve reliability.

- Work closely with mechanical, electronics, software, and automation engineers to develop integrated experimental systems.

- Troubleshoot complex technical problems across chemistry, hardware, and process engineering.

- Develop analytical methods and quality control strategies to measure performance and guide optimization.

- Help scale successful prototypes into robust, reproducible systems suitable for routine production.

- Work with external suppliers and engineering partners to source components, evaluate technologies, and accelerate development.

What We're Looking For

- A strong background in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience designing, building, and testing experimental setups, prototypes, or laboratory equipment.

- Strong understanding of chemistry, materials, or process engineering, with the ability to apply these fundamentals to practical engineering challenges.

- Experience developing and optimizing experimental processes, including systematic troubleshooting and performance characterization.

- Comfortable working across hardware and experimental science, translating scientific requirements into practical engineering solutions.

- Experience selecting components, evaluating technical trade-offs, and iterating on prototype designs.

- Strong experimental skills, including designing experiments, analyzing data, and making decisions based on results.

- Independent, resourceful, and comfortable working on open-ended technical problems.

- A practical, hands-on approach to engineering, with a focus on building, testing, and improving systems rather than purely theoretical development.

- Experience with DNA or oligonucleotide synthesis, including chemical or enzymatic approaches, is a plus.

- Experience with solid-phase synthesis, surface chemistry, or chemical process development is a plus.

- Familiarity with microfluidics, high-throughput dispensing, or array-based technologies is a plus.

- Experience with laboratory automation, instrumentation, or custom hardware development is a plus.

- Experience with CAD, electronics, fluidics, or mechanical prototyping is a plus.

- Experience scaling experimental technologies from proof of concept to production is a plus.

- Programming and data analysis experience, particularly in Python, is a plus.

title: Senior Cryogenic Engineer
description:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance .

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. 

What to Expect 

We are seeking a Senior Cryogenic Engineer to support and develop advanced cryogenic platforms for our SNSPD (Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detector) product line, with a strong emphasis on next-generation rack-mountable systems.

You will join a cross-functional team dedicated to advancing world-class quantum technologies that address some of the most complex challenges in computing, networking, and sensing. title: Quantitative Researcher - 2027 Graduates
description:
At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?

As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.

This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.

Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

What You'll Work On

You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:

- Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events

- Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them

- Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading

- Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise

- Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible

- Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales

- Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models

- Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper

- Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems

- Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge

No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.

What Success Looks Like

Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.

- Degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics, operations research or machine learning

- No active backlogs

- Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++

- Solid grounding in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects

- Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking

- A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.

Our Culture

More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to keep asking why, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to pursue difficult problems, intellectually honest enough to abandon an idea when the evidence says so, and humble enough to keep learning.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. You'll have meaningful ownership of research problems from day one: forming your own hypotheses, challenging existing approaches and following the evidence wherever it leads, with the infrastructure and datasets to test ideas at scale, competitive compensation, and a culture where the best idea wins regardless of who proposed it.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created, and they never stop changing. Neither should our thinking. Every day, someone asks a better question and finds an answer nobody had. That someone could be you.

title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
description:
Wat ga je doen? 

Samen met de CEO en COO werk je aan de verdere strategische en financiële ontwikkeling van de organisatie. Als CFO vertaal je de ondernemingsstrategie naar concrete groeikansen door schaalbare verdien- en prijsmodellen te ontwikkelen. Per markt, regio, entiteit, businessunit en klantsegment analyseer je waar kansen liggen, op basis van verwachte klantwaarde, omzetpotentieel, kosten, marge, cashflow, risico en schaalbaarheid. Deze inzichten verwerk je in businesscases waarin zowel het perspectief van de klant als van Voortman Steel Machinery naar voren komen. 

Daarnaast ontwikkel je heldere investeringskaders en breng je passende financieringsmodellen in kaart die aansluiten op de aard van de activiteiten en de internationale context. Daarbij weeg je beschikbare financieringsopties zorgvuldig af op impact, liquiditeit en rendement. Op basis daarvan adviseer je de board over prioriteiten en zorg je dat middelen terechtkomen bij de initiatieven die het meest bijdragen aan de strategische en financiële doelstellingen van Voortman Steel Machinery. Als onderdeel hiervan bepaal je ook onder welke financiële en organisatorische voorwaarden pilots kunnen worden gestart en opgeschaald. Met heldere go/no-go-momenten per fase zorg je ervoor dat de ontwikkeling en implementatie van nieuwe verdien- en prijsmodellen niet sneller gaat dan wat de organisatie kan adopteren. Daarnaast monitor je de financiële resultaten van nieuwe verdien- en prijsmodellen en bepaal je of de uitrol moet worden versneld, voortgezet, bijgestuurd of afgeschaald. Tegelijkertijd borg je dat contracten allesomvattende afspraken en een evenwichtige risicoverdeling bevatten, evenals uitvoerbaar zijn in alle landen waar Voortman Steel Machinery actief is. Zo werk je gericht aan verdien- en prijsmodellen die commercieel aantrekkelijk, financieel gezond en schaalbaar zijn. 

Als CFO draag je actief bij aan de verdere internationale groei van Voortman Steel Machinery. Hiervoor ontwikkel je strategische, financiële en organisatorische plannen, zodat per markt en internationale entiteit helder is welke inrichting het beste past bij de gewenste groei. Daarbij verzorg je de afstemming tussen verschillende afdelingen en entiteiten, zonder de lijnverantwoordelijkheid van collega's over te nemen. Tevens bewaak je per land en internationale entiteit het rendement, de cashflow, het werkkapitaal en houd je zicht op financiële, juridische, fiscale, contractuele en compliance-risico’s. 

Ook de financiële besturing en beheersing van Voortman Steel Machinery valt onder jouw verantwoordelijkheid. Je bent internationaal eindverantwoordelijk voor consolidatie, planning & control, reporting, accounting, treasury, audit, tax, vennootschapsbelasting en interne beheersing. Aansluitend zie je toe op het opstellen van correcte en transparante rapportages per internationale entiteit. De dagelijkse coördinatie van deze verschillende activiteiten en de aansturing van de Finance-afdeling wordt verzorgd door de Finance-director, waarmee je nauw samenwerkt. Jij fungeert als sparringpartner, stuurt bij waar nodig, bewaakt de strategisch richting van de Finance-afdeling, verzorgt correcte governance en behandeld onderwerpen met board impact. Tevens ben je het gezicht van Voortman Steel Machinery richting banken, verzekeraars, accountant en andere financiële stakeholders. 

Wat maakt deze rol uniek? 

In deze rol krijg je de kans om zichtbaar richting te geven aan de volgende groeifase van Voortman Steel Machinery. Je komt terecht in een organisatie waar ondernemerschap, innovatie en slagkracht samenkomen: ideeën worden niet alleen verkend, maar ook scherp getoetst op waardecreatie, rendement, risico en schaalbaarheid. Daarmee krijg je ruimte om jouw financiële expertise en strategisch vermogen in te zetten bij het ontwikkelen van nieuwe proposities, het onderbouwen van businesscases en het bepalen van investeringskeuzes die impact hebben op de internationale groei van de organisatie. Dit maakt de functie nadrukkelijk méér dan een traditionele CFO-rol: je bewaakt niet alleen de financiële basis, maar bent medebepalend in hoe Voortman Steel Machinery commerciële kansen vertaalt naar gezonde, schaalbare en toekomstbestendige groei. 

Positie binnen de organisatie 

Voortman Steel Machinery ontwikkelt machines, software en serviceoplossingen waarmee staalverwerkende bedrijven hun productieprocessen automatiseren en optimaliseren. Het hoofdkantoor is gevestigd in Nederland. Dankzij vestigingen in verschillende landen kan effectieve lokale ondersteuning worden geboden. De recent geopende, grootschalige productielocatie in de Verenigde Staten laat zien hoe de organisatie internationaal blijft groeien. Tevens vindt in Engeland hoofdzakelijk de ontwikkeling van onze LogicSteel-software plaats. Daarnaast bezit Voortman wereldwijd diverse sales & service-hubs. 

Als CFO vorm je samen met de CEO en COO de board van Voortman Steel Machinery, geef je met hen richting aan de ontwikkeling van het Global Management Team en de organisatie als geheel. Jouw focus ligt op het vertalen van de ondernemingsstrategie naar concrete kansen voor nieuwe verdien- en prijsmodellen. Hierbij werk je intensief samen met de afdeling Product Management, dat verantwoordelijk is voor het identificeren en ontwikkelen van software-, machine- en serviceproposities. Als CFO ben je eindverantwoordelijk voor de Finance-afdeling en werk je nauw samen met de Finance Director, die de dagelijkse internationale operationele aansturing van de afdeling verzorgt. Tevens rapporteren de HR-Manager en Trade Compliance Officer aan jou. De HR-Manager is (mede) verantwoordelijk voor het ontwikkelen van de HR-strategie en het borgen van de operationele uitvoering. Daarnaast ziet de Trade Compliance Officer erop toe dat de organisatie voldoet aan de relevante wet- en regelgeving. Daarbij bewaakt de Trade Compliance Officer onder andere de inhoudelijke juistheid en werking van ingezette maatregelen. 

Wat wij bieden? 

Bij Voortman Steel Machinery kom je terecht in een écht familiebedrijf met een informele, betrokken en ondernemende cultuur. Mensen kennen elkaar en lijnen zijn kort. Er is volop ruimte om verantwoordelijkheid te nemen, initiatief te tonen en ideeën verder te brengen. Onze kernwaarden ondernemerschap, vakmanschap, passie voor technologie, toewijding en samenwerking vormen daarbij de basis voor hoe we werken en met elkaar omgaan. Je ziet ze terug in de trots waarmee we hoogwaardige technologie ontwikkelen, in de manier waarop teams elkaar versterken en in de gezamenlijke drive om klanten vooruit te helpen. Zo ontstaat een werkomgeving waarin ambitie, betrokkenheid en werkplezier op een natuurlijke manier samenkomen. 

Naast een professionele, ondernemende en loyale werkomgeving krijg je bij ons: 

- Een marktconform salaris, passend bij jouw kennis en ervaring; 

- Een passende pensioenregeling bij ASR, waarbij jij en Voortman samen pensioenkapitaal opbouwen; 

- Een leaseauto voor zakelijk en privégebruik; 

- Een sleutelrol in het realiseren van onze strategie met internationale impact; 

- Werken in een moderne omgeving op onze Voortman Campus in Rijssen; 

Wat breng je mee? 

Wij zoeken een ondernemende, strategische en daadkrachtige CFO met een afgeronde masteropleiding in Finance, Economie, Bedrijfskunde of een vergelijkbare richting. Een titel als RA, RC of CPA is een must. Je hebt minimaal vijf jaar ervaring als CFO, Divisie-CFO, Senior Finance Director, Head of Finance of Director Corporate Finance, bij voorkeur binnen een internationale original equipment manufacturer (OEM), industrieel technologiebedrijf, technisch complexe B2B-organisatie of top-tier consultancybureau. Ervaring binnen een ondernemend familiebedrijf of een organisatie van vergelijkbare omvang en complexiteit is daarbij een pré. Daarnaast heb je ervaring met aansturen van een finance-afdeling of -team. Verder voldoe je aan het volgende profiel: 

- Strategisch en analytisch vermogen: je beschikt over sterk analytisch en strategisch vermogen en hebt aantoonbare ervaring met het doorgronden van complexe data en businessmodellen. Je weet informatie te vertalen naar heldere strategische en financiële logica, logische transparante aannames en goed onderbouwde besluitvorming. Je bent in staat om richting te bepalen, langetermijndoelen te formuleren en de organisatie daarin mee te nemen. 

- Businessmodelinnovatie: je hebt aantoonbare ervaring met het in kaart brengen van groeikansen en het ontwikkelen van nieuwe (schaalbare) verdien-, prijs- en contractmodellen. Deze weet je te onderbouwen met solide businesscases en scenarioanalyses. Daarnaast heb je ruime ervaring met het ontwikkelen van financieringsmodellen en het inrichten van kapitaalallocatie op basis van het (verwachte) rendement, risico’s en strategische bijdrage. 

- Besluitvaardig en resultaatgericht: je bent besluitvaardig en kunt tijdig en doordacht keuzes maken op basis van beschikbare informatie. Als je éénmaal een keuze hebt gemaakt, durf je achter je keuze te blijven staan. Je beschikt over overtuigingskracht, kunt draagvlak creëren en interne en externe stakeholders zorgvuldig meenemen in strategische veranderingen. Tevens stuur je actief op concrete resultaten en realiseer je aantoonbare positieve financiële impact. 

- Verandervermogen en omgevingsbewustzijn: je hebt ervaring met het realiseren van interne veranderingen en de implementatie van nieuwe verdien- en prijsmodellen, evenals het tijdig bijsturen daarvan. Tevens ben je sterk in het vertalen van nieuwe verdien- en prijsmodellen naar heldere, beheersbare processen en rollen. Daarbij zorg je voor een gestructureerde stapsgewijze implementatie en ben je sterk in het meenemen en begeleiden van collega’s tijdens veranderingen. Ook onder druk en in complexe situaties blijf je rustig, behoud je overzicht en kun je snel schakelen. Tevens heb je een scherp oog voor verhoudingen, kun je belangen goed afwegen en anticipeer je tijdig op ontwikkelingen. Daarbij heb je een goed begrip van culturele en organisatorische verschillen in een internationale context. 

- Verbindend vermogen en communicatie: je bent betrokken en weet duurzame professionele relaties op te bouwen en te onderhouden met interne en externe stakeholders, zoals banken, accountants en verzekeraars. Je communiceert helder, informeert betrokkenen tijdig over relevante ontwikkelingen en bent benaderbaar. Je weet complexe onderwerpen begrijpelijk over te brengen en stemt je communicatie af op verschillende gesprekspartners. Daarnaast beschik je over sterke Nederlandse en Engelse communicatieve vaardigheden, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. 

- Inspirerend leiderschap: jouw leiderschap is gericht op groei, vertrouwen en ontwikkeling. Je weet medewerkers te coachen, te inspireren en richting te geven, terwijl je ruimte geeft voor eigenaarschap en verantwoordelijkheid. Daarbij stuur je bij waar nodig, stimuleer je samenwerking en help je collega’s hun potentieel te benutten. Zo draag je bij aan een omgeving waarin mensen zich betrokken voelen en werken aan gezamenlijke doelen. 

- Onafhankelijke en reflectieve houding: je hebt een onafhankelijke, kritische en constructieve houding, staat open voor feedback, kunt je eigen handelen kritisch evalueren en wilt continu blijven leren. 

Nieuwsgierig? 

Ben jij dé ondernemende en daadkrachtige Chief Financial Officer (CFO) die strategie weet te vertalen naar waarde, nieuwe verdienmodellen tot leven brengt, internationale groei mede realiseert en de organisatie met visie en resultaatgerichtheid stuurt? Solliciteer dan nu en word onderdeel van onze organisatie! Na ontvangst beoordelen wij jouw sollicitatie en nemen we binnen twee werkdagen contact met je op. Zijn wij net als jij positief, dan nodigen we je graag uit voor een eerste sollicitatiegesprek op locatie. Bij een positieve uitkomst volgt een tweede en mogelijk derde sollicitatiegesprek. title: Sales Director (International), OTE €150.000 per year | Breda
description:
You hit targets. But what you really want is to build. 

You know how to deliver ARR targets. What really gets you going is building a sales organisation that’s ready for the next stage of growth. Sound like you? Read on. 

Your role
As Sales Director, you’re the CCO’s operational and tactical right hand on sales management. The CCO holds ultimate responsibility for the group result and the strategic relationships. You make sure we deliver our ARR targets, day in, day out. You keep the sales team sharp, focused and on track. Customer Success and expansion also fall under your leadership.

This is explicitly more than running today’s team. You help build tomorrow’s. You translate the group’s growth strategy (vertical specialisation, internationalisation and portfolio expansion) into the commercial capacity and structure we’ll need next. You also help build the playbook that lets sales teams from new acquisitions integrate smoothly into the group.

You report to the CCO. Together with the CCO and the Marketing Director, you form the Commercial MT (CMT). You also work closely with the Leadership Team (LT).

Day to day, you and the Marketing Director make sure the commercial disciplines work together seamlessly: from lead to pipeline to revenue. You make clear agreements on MQLs, SQLs and forecasting. That collaboration has to be ultra-tight.

What you’ll do 
Revenue & results

You’re operationally responsible for delivering the group’s ARR targets, day in, day out. That covers new business, upsell and cross-sell, and retention and expansion through Customer Success.

You translate the commercial strategy (set with and by the CCO and the Commercial MT) into concrete sales goals, targets per country and team, and an actionable sales plan.

You drive pipeline, conversion and forecast accuracy. You own the sales funnel from SQL to closed-won, and the expansion funnel within our existing customer base.

You’re responsible for pricing and deal structure within the agreed framework, in line with our margin and growth targets.

Leadership & team 
+ You lead and further professionalise the sales team (about 15 FTE) day to day, across all countries where Whitevision operates. That includes visiting our offices and teams at the various locations.
+ You directly lead Customer Success (currently 2 FTE) as part of the broader sales and expansion motion. As the team grows, this structure can grow with it.
+ You decide on team structure, capacity and how accounts and verticals are divided, to fit our international growth.
+ You coach, develop and recruit sales professionals. You also own onboarding and enablement for new colleagues.
+ You drive individual and team performance with clear KPIs and a healthy rhythm of 1:1s, forecast reviews and pipeline meetings.

Building & integrating
+ You set up and safeguard scalable sales processes, CRM and tooling that grow with a fast-growing, international buy-and-build organisation.
+ You own the sales methodology, from qualification through negotiation to closing. You make sure every country and team applies it the same way.
+ You (co-)develop and execute the playbook for integrating sales teams of newly acquired companies: one sales methodology, one CRM, one way of working.
+ You spot operational bottlenecks in the commercial organisation and resolve them.

Collaboration & execution
+ You work closely with the Marketing Director on lead follow-up, campaign ROI, events, partners and a consistent go-to-market.
+ You support the CCO in the commercial execution of strategic partnerships, including AFAS, 4PS, Exact and other partners.
+ You report on sales performance, pipeline and risks to the CCO and the Commercial MT.
+ You travel regularly to our international teams and customers.

About Whitevision 

Whitevision is a fast-growing SaaS organisation. We specialise in intelligent document processing and automating document-intensive workflows. Through an ambitious buy-and-build strategy, we’re bringing several software companies together into one strong, international platform. We’re active across Europe, and the US is likely next.

Our mission is clear: build one strong, recognisable and scalable company. One Company. The coming years are all about international growth, integration and commercial professionalisation. For this next phase, we’re looking for a Sales Director who doesn’t just deliver results, but also builds the organisation that makes the next stage of growth possible.

"At Whitevision, we provide a solution that genuinely helps people move forward in their organizations. It enables them to work more efficiently and effectively, allowing them to make a greater impact. Our team is stable and consists of a great mix of experience, personalities, and backgrounds. That diversity is one of our strengths. We also enjoy spending time together outside of work, whether it's a game of padel or a limoncello workshop." Erik, Sales Manager 

What you bring
+ 2–4 years of sales management experience, including at least one year in an end-responsible role (Sales Director or Head of Sales) in B2B SaaS or software.
+ A successful track record of at least 4 years as an individual contributor in SaaS sales.
+ A proven track record of hitting MRR/ARR targets and scaling a sales team in a fast-growing environment.
+ Experience (co-)building a sales organisation. You’ve put structure, process and capacity in place for the next phase, not just run an existing team.
+ You’re data- and process-driven. You build processes, rhythm and discipline, and you steer on data and forecasts.
+ An affinity for Customer Success and retention, alongside new business sales.
+ Experience leading sales teams across multiple countries and cultures. You’re a leader people want to follow, and the teams you’ve led will tell you so.
+ Experience in a scale-up or buy-and-build SaaS environment is a strong plus.
+ You’re a natural sparring partner for marketing. You think in terms of the full funnel, not just your own team.
+ Excellent English. Good Dutch is a plus, as is fluency in a third European language.

Our Whitevision way of working is built on respect, decisiveness, commitment and ambition. These core values are an excellent match with your personality and the way you approach your work. 

What we offer
+ OTE of €150,000 per year, depending on your experience. We’ll discuss the split, accelerators and caps on the variable part together.

+ An executive role with direct, operational impact on our commercial result and on building a fast-growing international SaaS organisation.
+ Close collaboration in a small, decisive Commercial MT: the CCO, the Marketing Director and you.
+ The chance to help build tomorrow’s Sales and Customer Success organisation, including integrating new acquisitions.

Ready to drive our commercial engine?
Are you the Sales Director who’ll drive Whitevision’s commercial engine? Can you see yourself forming the Commercial MT with the CCO and the Marketing Director? Then we’d love to hear from you.

title: Director of Pricing & Monetization
description:
The world of payment processing is rapidly evolving, and businesses are looking for loyal and strategic partners, to help them grow.

Meet Nuvei , the Canadian fintech company accelerating the business of clients around the world. Nuvei's modular, flexible and scalable technology allows leading companies to accept next-gen payments, offer all payout options and benefit from card issuing, banking, risk and fraud management services. Connecting businesses to their customers in more than 200 markets, with local acquiring in 50 markets, 150 currencies and 700 alternative payment methods, Nuvei provides the technology and insights for customers and partners to succeed locally and globally with one integration.

At Nuvei, we live our core values, and we thrive on solving complex problems. We’re dedicated to continually improving our product and providing relentless customer service. We are always looking for exceptional talent to join us on the journey!

Your Mission 

We are looking for a Director of Pricing & Monetization , who will be responsible for defining and executing the company's pricing strategy to maximize revenue growth, profitability, and market competitiveness. This leader will develop scalable pricing frameworks, design bundled product offerings, lead willingness-to-pay research, and establish a data-driven approach to pricing across products, industries, customer segments, and geographies. The role sits at the intersection of Commercial, Marketing, Finance, Data Analytics & Product, ensuring pricing decisions balance customer value, competitive positioning, profitability, and growth objectives. 

Responsibilities 

Pricing Framework Development 

- Design and maintain the company's enterprise-wide pricing framework. 
- Develop attribute-based pricing models across products, industries, geographies, customer segments, and risk profiles. 
- Establish pricing governance, policies, guardrails, and decision-making frameworks. 
- Create methodologies for standard pricing, exception pricing, strategic discounts, and deal approvals. 
- Define pricing architecture for new products and market launches. 
Bundling & Monetization Strategy 

- Design and implement bundled product and service offerings that maximize customer value and company profitability. 
- Identify opportunities to unbundle and re-bundle products to improve monetization and customer segmentation. 
- Develop packaging strategies across core products, value-added services, premium features, and subscriptions. 
- Partner with Product Management to create tiered "Good-Better-Best" pricing structures. 
- Measure bundle performance and continuously optimize package economics. 
Willingness-to-Pay & Customer Research 

- Lead willingness-to-pay studies and pricing research programs.

description:
Utrecht | Strategisch leiderschap | 38,75 uur 

Maak het verschil als managing director bij Berenschot 

Nederland staat voor één van de grootste transities van deze generatie. De energietransitie, de druk op de leefomgeving, netcongestie, woningbouw, stikstof, klimaatadaptatie en ruimtelijke ordening vragen om nieuwe vormen van samenwerking tussen overheid, bedrijfsleven en maatschappelijke organisaties. Al 85 jaar helpt Berenschot als toonaangevend adviesbureau opdrachtgevers om in complexiteit richting te bepalen en resultaten te realiseren. Als managing director Energie & Leefomgeving speel je hierin een sleutelrol. Je bepaalt mede de koers van onze grootste maatschappelijke adviespraktijken en draagt bij aan de toekomst van Nederland. Heb jij ervaring in een van deze domeinen in de consultancy of als leidinggevende bij een van onze opdrachtgevers? Heb jij een sterk netwerk op C-level en ben je commercieel gedreven zonder de maatschappelijke opgave uit het oog te verliezen? Dan is dit jouw kans om het verschil te maken als managing director Energie & Leefomgeving bij Berenschot. 

Dit ga je doen 

Als managing director en tevens lid van het mt draag je actief bij aan de (uitvoering van de) strategie van Berenschot en ben je verantwoordelijk voor de strategierealisatie en financiële prestaties van de adviesgroep Energie & Leefomgeving (E&L). Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor een van de grootste adviesgroepen binnen Berenschot met circa zeventig professionals en een substantiële omzetbijdrage aan de groep. Je leidt het E&L-managementteam met vijf teamleads en draagt bij aan de verdere positionering en groei van Berenschot in de betreffende domeinen, voortbouwend op onze sterke reputatie. Je geeft richting aan de volgende groeifase binnen energie en leefomgeving, inspelend op de veranderende markt, waarin ook digitalisering en realisatie steeds belangrijker worden. Het zwaartepunt ligt hierbij op het goed positioneren van de adviesgroep Energie & Leefomgeving bij onze klanten buiten en het intern leiden van de E&L-teams naar de volgende fase. 

- Je hebt een heldere visie op de ontwikkelingen in de energiesector en de leefomgeving. Je kent onze opdrachtgevers, begrijpt hun vraagstukken en vertaalt dit samen met je teams naar een scherpe strategische koers, met commerciële kansen buiten en een strategisch personeelsplan binnen. 

- Je ondersteunt marktteams bij het ontwikkelen van nieuwe business en initieert, ontwikkelt en realiseert omvangrijke adviesopdrachten en strategische samenwerkingen. 

- Je onderhoudt en versterkt relaties op C-level binnen relevante klantsegmenten voor E&L: (netbeheerders, energieproducenten, warmtebedrijven, ministeries van EZK, IenW en LVVN, provincies en waterschappen). 

- Je bent een gezaghebbende gesprekspartner binnen het publieke debat op ten minste een van de proposities van E&L en begrijpt de context van het gehele veld, waarbinnen E&L opereert. Je vertegenwoordigt Berenschot in bestuurlijke netwerken, media, congressen en vakinhoudelijke platforms. 

- Je geeft niet alleen richting aan de groep met haar diverse teams, maar bouwt met de groep aan de volgende fase van E&L. 

- Je bent zichtbaar en benaderbaar op de werkvloer en legt verbinding. Je ondersteunt teamleads en professionals en daagt hen uit in hun ontwikkeling. 

- Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het opstellen en realiseren van een begroting, stuurt op declarabiliteit, bezettingsgraad en rendement. 

Als lid van het Berenschot-mt beïnvloed je niet alleen de ontwikkeling van de adviesgroep Energie & Leefomgeving, maar draag je medeverantwoordelijkheid voor de strategische koers, groei en cultuur van Berenschot als geheel. 

Dit neem je mee 

Je bent een zeer ervaren en bewezen succesvolle adviseur en/of leidinggevende met een scherp strategisch inzicht en een intrinsieke motivatie om bij te dragen aan de transities waaraan Energie & Leefomgeving werkt. 

De ideale kandidaat voor de functie: 

- Heeft een afgeronde universitaire masteropleiding. 

- Beschikt over minimaal vijftien jaar relevante werkervaring als adviseur, leidinggevende of eindverantwoordelijke manager binnen consultancy, overheid, energie, infrastructuur of leefomgeving en heeft affiniteit met de maatschappelijke opgaven waaraan we werken. 

- Heeft commerciële slagkracht en een stevig netwerk binnen de domeinen van de adviesgroep Energie & Leefomgeving. Je hebt aantoonbare succesvolle ervaring in het initiëren, ontwikkelen en realiseren van omvangrijke adviesopdrachten en strategische samenwerkingen. 

- Kent de dynamiek van een professional services firm, is energiek en weet kortetermijndynamiek te verbinden met een langetermijnontwikkeling. 

- Heeft innovatiekracht en is ondernemend ingesteld. Je bent een positief-kritische en strategische sparringpartner die op nieuwe zaken durft te anticiperen en vanuit helicopterview zaken verder weet te brengen. 

- Voelt zich thuis in complexe en uitdagende opdrachten op hoog bestuurlijk/ambtelijk niveau, heeft een proactieve houding, gevoel voor sociale processen en kan goed samenwerken. 

- Heeft bewezen leiderschapskwaliteiten in een professionele en bij voorkeur ook commerciële kennisomgeving. Je hebt flair, toont lef en daadkracht, en blijft daarbij in verbinding met de organisatie en betrokken opdrachtgevers. 

- Bent zichtbaar en benaderbaar voor professionals. Je weet talent aan je te binden en creëert verbinding in het E&L-managementteam en met professionals in de organisatie. Je motiveert en creëert draagvlak; niet vanuit macht maar vanuit natuurlijke verbinding. 

- Stimuleert samenwerking tussen disciplines en zoekt actief samenwerking op met collega-MD’s. 

Dit zijn je directe collega’s 

Berenschot is een zelfstandig en onafhankelijk Nederlands organisatieadviesbureau in Utrecht, waar we met meer dan 500 gedreven collega’s werken aan duurzame oplossingen voor de vraagstukken van onze opdrachtgevers. We dragen bij aan vooruitgang in organisaties en de maatschappij met onze adviezen en oplossingen. We streven altijd naar verrassende en vernieuwende oplossingen, wat ons uniek maakt. Berenschot kenmerkt zich door een open en informele cultuur, samenwerking tussen verschillende vakgebieden en veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid. 

Dit bieden we jou 

Berenschot is een informele, slagvaardige organisatie met korte communicatielijnen waar er echt naar je wordt geluisterd. Er zijn volop mogelijkheden voor persoonlijke en professionele groei waarbij jouw initiatief wordt omarmd en gefaciliteerd. Je hebt hier de vrijheid om te ondernemen. Ons inclusieve personeelsbeleid omarmt diversiteit en biedt iedereen gelijke kansen.

Je komt in een betrokken en ambitieus team, dat aan de meest relevante maatschappelijke opgaven en transities werkt in de energiesector en in de leefomgeving. Je landt in een steward owned organisatie die altijd streeft naar maatschappelijke impact. Een organisatie waarin je ruimte krijgt om te ondernemen en om zelf initiatieven te ontwikkelen. 

Natuurlijk hebben we daarnaast ook uitstekende arbeidsvoorwaarden en geweldige ontwikkelmogelijkheden: 

• Een vast jaarinkomen ligt tussen de € 135K-€ 180K, afhankelijk van ervaring. 

• Een variabele beloning (bonusregeling), afhankelijk van prestaties. 

• Een winstdelingsregeling. 

• Een representatievergoeding. 

• 27 vakantiedagen. 

• Een mobiliteitsbudget waarbinnen je onder andere een auto kunt leasen. 

• Een uitstekende pensioenregeling. 

• Flexibele werktijden en de mogelijkheid om hybride te werken. 

• Een positie in een betrokken en ambitieus team. 

• Een organisatie waarin je ruimte krijgt om te ondernemen en zelf initiatieven te ontwikkelen. 

Solliciteer meteen 

Wil jij ook impact maken bij Berenschot? Stuur ons dan zo snel mogelijk, maar uiterlijk 1 november 2026, jouw cv en motivatie. Solliciteer eenvoudig via onderstaande solliciteerbutton. Heb je inhoudelijke vragen over de functie, neem dan contact op met Madelon van den Hoven (hr-manager ) of Marinke Wijngaard (directeur ). 

Zo ziet het sollicitatieproces eruit 

Na je sollicitatie ontvang je binnen enkele dagen een reactie. Bij een positieve uitkomst nodigen we je uit voor een kennismaking met collega’s uit jouw team en je toekomstige manager. De gesprekken vinden plaats vanaf 9 november 2026. Als de gesprekken goed verlopen, volgt er een assessment. Blijkt daaruit dat jij een echte Berenschotter bent? Dan doen we je een concreet aanbod. Hierna heten we je graag welkom in ons team.

title: Senior iOS Developer (Remote)
description:
About Finom 

Finom is a European tech startup headquartered in Amsterdam, and we’re on a journey towards revolutionizing the financial landscape for entrepreneurs worldwide. Our mission is to develop an all-in-one financial B2B solution that integrates banking functions, accounting, financial management, and invoicing into a seamless, mobile-first platform.

We recently closed a €115 million Series C equity round (around $133 million), bringing our total funding to approximately $346 million. This significant investment follows a $105 million growth funding round from General Catalyst, a long-term backer since 2021 known for supporting companies like Airbnb, HubSpot, KAYAK, and Stripe.

Finom's platform goes beyond traditional banking, offering invoicing and a growing suite of features, including AI-enabled accounting, aiming to simplify financial management for entrepreneurs. We're actively expanding our reach across key EU markets like Germany, France, the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain.

At Finom, we’re not just redefining the entrepreneurial experience — we’re empowering our employees to make a real difference. Your work matters, and your impact extends far beyond product metrics. We nurture innovation and an inspiring work environment where bold ideas thrive, prioritizing thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and our business as a whole.

Maintaining our start-up spirit, we prioritize thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and, of course, our business.

The Role 

For hundreds of thousands of European entrepreneurs, our iOS app is Finom. It's how they check their cash flow over morning coffee, approve a payment between client meetings, and freeze a card the moment something looks off. We're mobile-first by conviction, not convenience — the app isn't a companion to the "real" product; it is the product. And as an AI-native platform, the features you build increasingly carry intelligence inside them: AI-powered accounting, smart categorization, and agentic workflows that quietly save business owners hours every week. When you ship something great, someone somewhere feels it the same day. 

That's why we're not looking for someone to implement tickets. We're looking for a Senior Mobile (iOS) Engineer who thinks like a product builder — someone who cares deeply about the "why" behind what they're building, challenges assumptions when needed, and proactively spots opportunities to create better outcomes. 

You'll be embedded in a cross-functional domain team — Backend, Mobile, ML/AI, QA, Design, and Product — that owns a shared product area end-to-end. No handoff culture, no "not my layer": everyone in the team is solving the same customer problem, and you'll shape solutions from the first product conversation to the moment the feature is live in users' hands. Fewer silos means more flow — and real, end-to-end ownership. 

How We Build
