title: Medical Coder
description:
Who You Are

You are a detail-oriented, experienced medical coder who understands that accurate coding is the foundation of a healthy revenue cycle. You bring strong outpatient coding expertise and a sharp eye for documentation - catching what others miss and knowing exactly how to translate a clinical encounter into a clean, compliant claim. You communicate confidently with providers and teammates, and you know how to make complex coding questions easier to understand. You thrive in a remote environment where you can take ownership of your work, manage competing priorities, and keep things moving. Most importantly, you care about getting it right - for our providers, our patients, and the business.

Who We Are

Oasis Health Partners (Oasis) is building healthier communities by advancing primary care. We partner with patients, providers, and plans to provide personalized, local care for seniors across the country. We believe that patient needs come first, and that primary care is the foundation of patient-centric healthcare. With Oasis, patients receive better access and care. Providers receive the data, resources, and expertise to be successful in value-based care arrangements. Payors get the benefit of a solution that improves performance, drives growth, and reduces the total cost of care in hard-to-engage markets.

Together, we will boldly advance primary care for those that need it most. We are excited for you to join us on this journey. We invite you to be a part of Oasis, where you will discover we listen first, do the right thing, build things together and go all in --- while having fun!

Your Role

Oasis is building a strong, scalable Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) offering to support independent and community-based primary care practices. As a Medical Coder, you will play a vital role in keeping the revenue cycle moving - from accurate outpatient coding and clean claim submission through coding-related denial resolution. You will work closely with providers and billing staff to ensure documentation supports accurate, compliant coding, and serve as a resource when coding questions arise. Your work will help reduce revenue leakage, improve clean claim rates, and create a better experience for the practices and patients we serve.

Key Responsibilities

- Assign accurate CPT, ICD-10, and HCPCS codes for outpatient encounters based on provider documentation

- Enter and manage charges within eClinicalWorks (eCW)

- Review and submit claims, ensuring accuracy and compliance prior to submission

- Identify and resolve coding-related denials; resubmit corrected claims as needed

- Collaborate with providers and billing staff to clarify documentation and coding questions

- Stay current on payor policies, coding guideline updates, and compliance requirements

- Support coding audits and quality reviews as needed

Investment In Our Team

We invest in the personal and professional success of our team. We take care of our people and offer robust benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401k, and generous time off plans. We are committed to supporting your growth with a development program that starts with onboarding and continues throughout your career. As an inclusive, passionate, and diverse team, you will partner with professionals who understand the importance of high-value, high-impact patient care.

About You

- Certified Professional Coder (CPC) certification required

- Minimum 2 years of experience in outpatient medical coding

- Experience working in eClinicalWorks (eCW) preferred

- Strong working knowledge of CPT, ICD-10, HCPCS, and payor billing requirements

- Working knowledge of Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payor guidelines

- Strong attention to detail with a commitment to coding accuracy and compliance

- Ability to independently manage priorities and follow work through to resolution in a remote environment

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

- Reliable internet access and the ability to maintain a HIPAA-compliant remote workspace

Hourly Pay Range

$24—$29 USD

The salary range listed reflects the full compensation range for this role level at Oasis and is designed to support growth over time. description:
Coupa makes margins multiply through its community-generated AI and industry-leading total spend management platform for businesses large and small. Coupa AI is informed by trillions of dollars of direct and indirect spend data across a global network of 10M+ buyers and suppliers. We empower you with the ability to predict, prescribe, and automate smarter, more profitable business decisions to improve operating margins.

Why join Coupa?

Pioneering Technology: At Coupa, we're at the forefront of innovation, leveraging the latest technology to empower our customers with greater efficiency and visibility in their spend.

Collaborative Culture: We value collaboration and teamwork, and our culture is driven by transparency, openness, and a shared commitment to excellence.

We're looking for someone who's rebuilt a production system while it was running. CSP (Coupa Supplier Platform) serves millions of supplier companies—it's where they find work, receive orders, issue invoices, and get paid. The platform started as a Rails monolith. It works, but it needs to evolve. More traffic, more features, multi-cloud deployment, higher availability requirements.

You'll report to the VP of Engineering. CSP operates as a nimble team outside the larger engineering org, moving fast and pioneering approaches that demonstrate what's possible. You'll work with Ruby on Rails, Golang, Java—and introduce whatever else the architecture needs.

What You’ll Do 

- Lead the architectural evolution. Traffic is growing, functionality is expanding, robustness matters more than ever. You'll define what changes, in what order, and why.

- Set the patterns: API design, microservice boundaries, deployment pipelines, monitoring, reliability. Make them real, not theoretical.

- Mentor engineers. Guide decisions. Review architecture and code. Build the kind of team that ships ambitious work.

- Join the Architectural Steering Group. Share what you learn with Principal Engineers across Coupa. Import what works elsewhere.

- Partner with SRE on cloud-native infrastructure: CI/CD, containers, infrastructure-as-code, multi-cloud capabilities.

- Own security, multi-tenancy isolation, data governance, and compliance across all regions.

- Work with product, design, and business teams to turn supplier workflows into systems that scale.

What You Will Bring to Coupa 

- 15+ years building B2B SaaS at scale. You've held leadership and architectural roles where your decisions stuck around.

- Real experience evolving legacy systems into microservices—in production, with users depending on uptime.

- Deep knowledge of API-driven services, multi-tenant architectures, and B2B integration patterns that handle millions of users.

- Solid foundation in modern deployment: CI/CD, Docker/Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, working with cloud providers like AWS or GCP.

- Comfort across technology stacks (Rails, Golang, Java) and the judgment to pick tools that solve problems, not resume lines.

- Track record mentoring teams—providing direction without micromanaging, staying technical without bottlenecking.

- Problem-solving skills that balance scale, performance, technical debt, and shipping features. You know the trade-offs because you've lived them.

- Communication skills that work across engineering, product, and business. You build consensus without watering down hard truths.

title: Principal Sales Engineer - Canada
description:
At ExtraHop, we’re on a mission to protect and empower the connected enterprise. We reveal what is happening in the very infrastructure that sustains businesses, lives, and communities, and ensure the integrity of networks, data, systems, and processes. Organizations rely on ExtraHop to provide visibility into the cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and network performance issues that evade their existing security and IT tools. With this insight, organizations can investigate smarter, stop threats faster, and keep operations running.

Our mission is fueled by a profound social and moral responsibility to be the best at what we do, ensuring a secure world where everyone can thrive. If this sounds like a place you’d like to spend the next chapter of your career, we’d love to hear from you. 

Position Summary

As a Principal Sales Engineer, you will have a significant impact on the success of each sales presentation in which you participate and will share in its financial rewards. In this key position, you will contribute directly to the bottom-line health of the company.

As a Principal Sales Engineer, you will lead the technical sales strategy, deliver advanced product demonstrations, and guide customers through complex solution architectures. You’ll mentor other sales engineers, collaborate closely with product and engineering teams to align customer feedback with roadmap priorities, and support executive-level discussions. Your deep understanding of our technology, market landscape, and customer challenges will allow you to design and advocate for customer-tailored solutions that drive measurable business outcomes. Additionally, you will proactively resolve pre-sales technical challenges and act as a trusted advisor to both internal teams and customer stakeholders throughout the buying journey.

Key Responsibilities

- Complete mastery of all ExtraHop demo narratives

- Sufficiently versatile with the ExtraHop platform to conduct any ad-hoc demo upon request

- Key stakeholder in our demo creation/update process

- Maintain documents that are key to the SE workflow; deployment guidelines, POC best-practices, compelling use-cases, etc.

- Guide and mentor new ExtraHop SEs

- Recognized throughout the company as an expert in specific technologies/domains

- Recognized by peer SEs for their significant contributions that have benefited the broader SE community

- Ability to create and deliver public speaking sessions, blog posts, social media activity and analyst interactions.

- Interface with Product Management to relay market demands from prospects/customers and play a role in shaping the product roadmap

- Play an active role in the continuous refinement of our POC process; scoping questions/materials, output documents and best practices for aligning POC results to compelling business value

- Identify new areas of opportunity/revenue growth based on your customer/industry relationships and knowledge of the verticals we support

- Considers the business at-large when advocating for product/process changes and is able to assess the situation from the perspective of other organizations within the company 

- Actively drives changes to SE/company processes; comes up with an idea, vets it with peers/leadership, fleshes it out and leads the execution in concert with other internal stakeholders

- Expert-level understanding of the sales process; incorporates business requirements into the demo narrative, ensures POC outcomes are aligned with business impact, able to quickly/accurate qualify an opportunity

- Mastery of solution design; capable of translating customer input into a solution architecture that seamlessly aligns with the business proposal being developed by the RSM

Required Qualifications & Experience

- 10-14 years selling Cloud and Cyber Security technology into large Enterprises with direct AWS, Azure or GCP experience. 

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, or related area or demonstration of equivalent knowledge

- Minimum of 5 years of experience working directly with cloud concepts 

- Complex and strategic selling experience required

Skills & Competencies 

- Deep understanding of enterprise-architecture concepts, risk management, and excellent working knowledge of key protocols across Layers 2-7 (e.g., TCP/IP, HTTP, DNS, SSL/TLS, etc.).

- Expert level understanding of enterprise information technologies across the full OSI stack, cloud concepts (AWS, Azure, GCP).

- In-depth knowledge of Site Reliability Engineering Concepts

- Familiarity with automation and infrastructure as code technologies such as Ansible, Terraform, Cloud Formation

- Conducts highly complex work critical to the organisation

- Excellent organizational, interpersonal, and leadership skills, acts as a role model and a mentor for other sales engineers.

- Excellent communication (verbal and written) and presentation skills with the ability to interact and address Senior executive and technical audiences

- Ability to quickly learn new technologies and have an ongoing desire to stay current with the latest technologies

- Works without supervision with extensive latitude for independent judgement.

- Strong problem-solving skills: must be capable of accurately assessing needs, maintaining a calm business demeanor, and taking quick action to resolve issues

- Works cooperatively with others within the organization and other cross-functional stakeholders

- Works well in fast-paced, high-stress environments.

- Has predictable, reliable attendance.

The base salary range for this role is $180,000 to $190,000 CAD. This is a commission-eligible position with a 70/30 pay mix, for total target compensation of approximately $234,000 to $247,000 CAD at plan. Actual commission earnings are based on individual performance against quota.

ABOUT EXTRAHOP

ExtraHop is reinventing Network Detection and Response (NDR) to offer enterprises unparalleled visibility, context, and control against emerging threats. The platform integrates NDR with Network Performance Management (NPM), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and forensics, providing a single, comprehensive solution. By decrypting and analyzing complete packet-level data at wire speed and leveraging cloud-scale machine learning, ExtraHop empowers Security Operations Centers (SOCs) to detect, investigate, and remediate modern cyber risks in real time across their entire hybrid infrastructure, including data center, cloud, and SASE environments.

This comprehensive approach and market innovation have earned ExtraHop unique recognition as the only NDR vendor acknowledged as a leader by all major analyst firms, including the 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant for Network Detection and Response™, the 2025 Forrester® Wave for Network Analysis and Visibility, the 2024 IDC® Marketscape for NDR, and the 2025 Gigamon® Radar Report for Network Detection and Response. Since 2007, ExtraHop has consistently helped organizations worldwide extract in-depth network telemetry and contextual insights, affirming its commitment to protecting and empowering the connected enterprise.

OUR VALUES

Our culture is rooted in our five Values . These set the expectations for how we work individually and collectively as a team. 

Lead with Purpose: We are driven to deliver results that create a positive impact for our customers, partners, and colleagues.

title: Principal Data Scientist
description:
The Principal Data Scientist is the senior technical and scientific leader for AbbVie 's omnichannel engagement analytics, a data- and analytics-driven engagement optimization program spanning channel mix, content, field representative call planning, and orchestration. Operating within the APEX Enterprise Advanced Analytics and Innovation team, this role sets the multi-year science vision for personalized commercial engagement and is accountable for the technical strategy, methodology, and scientific rigor of the AI/ML and statistical solutions that power it. Reporting to the Associate Director, Data Science, the Principal is a thought partner to commercial and analytics leadership: shaping which problems are worth solving, forming and defending a point of view on how AI creates measurable business value, and partnering with product owners to turn that vision into scalable solutions. The role combines deep, hands-on expertise in applied machine learning, generative AI, causal inference, and experimentation with the consultative skill to align a complex stakeholder ecosystem around the right answer.

Key Responsibilities

- Define the Data Science vision: Own the multi-year Data Science vision and technical roadmap for omnichannel engagement analytics, anticipating where both the business and the field of AI are heading.

- Shape how AI creates business value: identify, size, and prioritize opportunities where AI can drive measurable commercial impact, build the business case, and influence senior leadership decisions on where to invest.

- Lead hands-on with Gen-AI: Personally use AI-assisted development and agentic tools to prototype, test hypotheses, and demonstrate value quickly; build LLM-backed systems using advanced RAG and context engineering, paired with rigorous scientific evaluation frameworks to scale highly reliable omnichannel recommendations.

- Lead the design of predictive and causal models: Develop next-best-action, recommendation, and sequential decision models that inform customer engagement and resource allocation using complex, multi-source data.

- Own measurement science: set the standard for measuring effectiveness, incrementality, and business impact using experimental and quasi-experimental methods, so that AI investments are evaluated rigorously.

- Partner with product owners to shape problems, not just fulfill requirements: co-define business outcomes, scope, and success metrics, and translate them into scalable technical solutions.

- Navigate a complex stakeholder ecosystem: build alignment across brand and marketing leaders, field sales and operations, Medical, Legal and Regulatory (MLR), Compliance, BTS, Digital Lab, and external vendors; reframe requests into well-posed problems and resolve competing priorities.

- Communicate with executive impact: translate complex methods and findings into clear recommendations and compelling narratives for executive and non-technical audiences.

- Productionize at scale: Partner with BTS, Digital Lab, engineering, and platform teams to deploy, monitor, and manage the lifecycle of AI/ML solutions.

- Raise the bar for scientific rigor: establish best practices in model development, code quality, reproducibility, peer review, and responsible AI across the data science community.

- Be a thought leader: stay at the forefront of research and practice in machine learning, generative AI, and causal inference; bring new ideas into the team; provoke rigorous analytical debate; and represent AbbVie 's point of view internally and in the broader analytics community.

Supervisory / Management Responsibilities

This role does not carry formal direct report responsibilities but is expected to act as a technical leader and mentor across the broader data science community, raising the bar on scientific rigor and hands-on AI practice. The Principal Data Scientist may lead technical workstreams with external analytics vendors and partners, including oversight of deliverable quality and methodology validation.

Key Competencies

- Scientific Engineering Depth: Deep expertise in machine learning, causal inference, and generative AI, combined with strong engineering discipline in reproducibility, deployment, and enterprise integration.

- AI Fluency and Bias to Action: Uses AI hands-on in daily work to prototype, analyze, and build; critically evaluates AI output; and turns ideas into working solutions quickly.

- Business Judgment and Problem-Framing: Translates ambiguous business challenges into well-scoped problems, connects technical choices to commercial value, and sets long-term technical direction while staying close to delivery.

- Stakeholder Navigation and Executive Influence: Reads organizational dynamics to build alignment across commercial, regulatory, and technology partners, earning trust as a thought partner to win support from senior leaders.

- Thought Leadership: Challenges conventional thinking and sparks meaningful analytical debate with peers and executives.

Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or another quantitative discipline required; Master’s or PhD in a quantitative field strongly preferred.

Required Experience

- 8+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, or applied science (or 6+ years with a PhD), with a track record of delivering production-quality models that drove measurable business impact.

- Demonstrated experience setting technical direction for a portfolio of AI/ML solutions and influencing decisions of senior business leaders.

- Experience building personalization, recommendation, decision-optimization, or marketing-science solutions, in any industry.

- Deep hands-on expertise in causal inference and experimentation, including A/B testing and quasi-experimental methods, to measure business impact.

- Demonstrated hands-on experience using generative AI and AI-assisted development tools (e.g., LLM APIs, AI coding assistants, agent frameworks) to prototype and deliver solutions, with concrete examples that can be walked through during the interview process.

- Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience in deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and distributed data processing.

- Experience productionizing AI/ML solutions in cloud environments, including deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management.

- Track record of leading initiatives across complex, cross-functional stakeholder environments and presenting to executive audiences.

Preferred Experience

- Commercial analytics experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, healthcare, or life sciences, including familiarity with data sources such as IQVIA, Symphony Health, APLD, or similar Rx, claims, and engagement data.

- Experience in omnichannel analytics, such as journey analysis, touchpoint measurement, closed-loop measurement, or next-best-action for HCP or patient engagement.

- Experience with advanced ML and optimization methods, including reinforcement learning, multi-armed bandits, transformers, and other approaches for sequential or recommendation use cases.

- Experience building LLM-based and agentic AI systems, including orchestration frameworks, evaluation, and integration through APIs and pipelines.

- Experience with cloud ML platforms and MLOps tools such as Azure ML, Databricks, and MLflow.

- External visibility through conference talks, publications, patents, open-source contributions, or recognized industry thought leadership.

title: Abuse Research Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote from the US

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

About the team

Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

Responsibilities

- Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.

- FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints. 

- Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows. 

- Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security. 

- Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls. 

Who you are 

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

Minimum requirements

- 5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains. 

- 5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems. 

- B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 

- Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines. 

- Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation methodologies. 

- Strong communication skills with a proven ability to translate complex technical research into clear, actionable recommendations and advisories for cross-functional partners.

Preferred qualifications 

- Deep technical understanding of threat actor motivations, infrastructure, and TTPs specific to financial fraud (e.g., ATO, Card Testing, Credential Stuffing). 

- Familiarity with standardized taxonomies such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&CK. 

- Proficiency with engineering, data processing, and analysis platforms such as Databricks, Trino, PySpark, Pandas, or Scikit-Learn. 

- Proven background utilizing Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs), tactical threat feeds, OSINT, and breach intelligence. 

- Demonstrated capability building or leveraging agentic LLM tools, automated testing systems, or control validation frameworks to model adversary behavior at scale. 

- Participation in industry conferences, webinars, or threat-sharing groups, alongside relevant professional certifications (e.g., GCTI, GCFA, OSCP).

We are hiring a Senior Risk Associate to run Lithic's risk assessment function: the client risk assessment program, the third party risk management program, and the enterprise risk assessment. - Own program underwriting: apply and maintain underwriting criteria, recommend spend, transfer, and reserve limits, and reassess programs as volume, product mix, and financial condition change.

- Run third party risk operations: vendor intake and tiering, due diligence and certification report review, control effectiveness ratings, the vendor risk register, annual reviews, and vendor issue and incident tracking.

- Support the enterprise risk assessment and the risk register: maintain the assessment inventory and calendar, collect and test control evidence, apply the enterprise rating methodology consistently across sub-assessments, and prepare Enterprise Risk Committee materials.

- Continuously improve the programs: refine rubrics, weights, questionnaires, and templates based on observed outcomes, and author and maintain the SOPs that make each assessment repeatable by someone other than you.

- Test, deploy, and tune agentic tooling across the assessment workflows, including document review, questionnaire analysis, vendor due diligence, and drafting, and document the context that makes the output repeatable and defensible.

- Define and report the KPIs and KRIs for the assessment programs, and surface concentration, trend, and thematic findings to leadership and oversight forums.

- Serve as the evidence owner for partner bank, audit, and examiner requests touching client, third party, and enterprise risk assessment.

- Mentor and cross-train teammates on assessment methodology, scoring discipline, and the tooling.

- Working knowledge of underwriting fundamentals: financial statement review, liquidity and runway analysis, loss and exposure monitoring, and limit setting.

- Fluency with rubric-based scoring methodologies and the discipline to apply them consistently and defend a rating.

- A track record of owning discrete risk programs end to end with limited guidance, including authoring the SOPs and defining the metrics that govern them.

You'll lead the team that builds the intelligence every ZoomInfo AI agent reasons over — what's true about companies and the people in them, how they relate, and what they're buying. This role owns the B2B data graph strategy end to end, blending classical machine learning and data science with LLM and agentic systems, and treating evaluation and inference cost as core disciplines. You'll set the technical bar for a team of senior engineers while staying close to the code, shipping alongside the people you lead.

What You'll Do 

- You will ship code alongside your team, prototype alone to prove or kill an idea, and review code as a peer, setting how the team uses agentic coding tools with precise specifications and rigorous review.

- You will own delivery end-to-end, from problem framing through serving and on-call, including long-tail graph coverage and user memory for agents that separates user-supplied context from system-of-record data.

- You will choose the right method for each problem — classical machine learning, language models, or code — for challenges like sparse-company revenue estimation, entity resolution, and semantic intent modeling, deciding on measured evidence and stopping work that won't pay off.

- You will define what it takes to claim an agent's output is correct, not just that its run completed, building the evaluation datasets, regression gates, and experiment designs that back those claims.

- You will own inference cost, latency, and capacity, including build-versus-buy and distillation decisions, since a model too expensive to run everywhere isn't a result.

- You will hire and grow machine learning engineers, data scientists, and research engineers, developing senior engineers into technical leaders.

- You will work across product, platform, security, and legal, and present results and their limits to executives, including when a system isn't good enough to launch.

What You Bring 

Must-Have: 

- You have significant experience building production machine learning systems and leading the engineers who build them by shipping alongside them — demonstrated capability matters more than years.

- You have a track record of hiring and developing senior machine learning engineers and data scientists against a high bar.

- You stay hands-on today: shipping code, building prototypes independently, and using agentic coding tools daily with rigorous review.

- You bring deep classical machine learning and data science expertise (supervised learning, feature engineering, statistical inference and experiment design, strong SQL) alongside production LLM and agentic systems, with the judgment to choose between them, including setting an evaluation bar with leakage-safe validation, calibration, and validated LLM judges.

- You have a record of cost and capacity decisions for model serving, such as moving a workload from a hosted model to a distilled or self-hosted one, with the savings measured, and you report results to executives with their limits stated, including recommending against a launch.

Preferred: 

- You bring entrepreneurial experience — founding a company, or taking a product from inception to paying customers as a founding or early engineer.

- You have experience in propensity modeling, ranking and retrieval, clustering, or entity resolution at scale.

- You have worked on web-scale language processing over multilingual, noisy text, knowledge graphs, or user memory for agents.

- You have experience with post-training and distillation, open-weight model serving, or AI governance and safety practices (ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF).

title: Senior Full Stack
description:
Headquarters: Tallinn, Estonia

URL: https://toggl.com/jobs/ 

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join one of our Product Tribes, the cross-functional units that own the end-to-end experience for a specific Toggl user role. You'll join the Tribe building for managers, the people who plan work, protect margins, and keep projects on time and on budget.

You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.

The salary for this position is €83,000 annually. 

You can work from anywhere in the world as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4. 

The Role 

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.

You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.

Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.

Your main responsibilities will be:

Ownership and delivery 

- 
Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.

- 
Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.

- 
Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.

Craft and quality across the stack 

- 
Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.

- 
Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.

- 
Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.

- 
Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.

Working with product and design 

- 
Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.

- 
Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.

- 
Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.

Raising the bar 

- 
Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.

- 
Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.

- 
Improve things across team boundaries. Spot shared components and duplicated work between Tribes, and raise it before we build the same thing twice.

AI as core leverage 

- 
Use AI tools extensively in your daily work for exploration, prototyping, code generation and review, debugging, research, and writing. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact - and you're expected to help the rest of the Tribe get better at it too.

About You 

You will thrive in this role if you:

- 
Have significant experience building and shipping production web applications end to end, and can lead major projects rather than just contribute to them.

- 
Are genuinely comfortable on both sides of the stack. You're deep on one side and properly capable on the other, not someone who hands off at the API boundary.

- 
Have deep, practical knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and modern CSS - including state management and side-effect handling in large applications.

- 
Are solid on backend fundamentals: at least one backend language you know well, API design, relational data modelling, and enough instinct for query performance to spot the problem before production does. Prior Golang experience is not mandatory but you have to be willing to adopt it and become comfortable with it fast. 

- 
Hold an extremely high bar for quality. You know what great looks like, you notice the details others miss, and you don't ship work you wouldn't put your name on.

- 
Have a knack for data-heavy product surfaces - performance, readability, and the principles behind a chart that actually communicates something.

- 
Care about the user's problem, not just the ticket. You start from what someone is trying to get done and work back to the implementation.

- 
Own outcomes, not output. You follow your work into production, watch how it behaves, and fix what needs fixing.

- 
Thrive in ambiguity and move fast. You make confident decisions with incomplete information, adapt when things change, and course-correct without drama.

- 
Are hands-on with AI tools. You actively use AI as a core part of how you build, not a side experiment, and you have opinions about where it helps and where it doesn't.

- 
Don't need to be managed. You set your own direction, keep people in the loop, and ask for help when it matters.

- 
Have excellent written and verbal English communication skills. You write clearly, explain technical tradeoffs to non-engineers without jargon, and default to async communication that others can follow.

- 
Are eager to contribute to the engineering team's growth - code review, mentoring, and interviewing included.

- 
Value transparency, ownership, and speed over perfection. You ship, learn, and improve rather than waiting for the perfect plan.

- 
Nice to have: 

- 
Experience with TanStack is a bonus, and so is a real understanding of frontend caching and eventual consistency, we'd love to hire someone who's dealt with that tradeoff directly.

- 
Experience with capacity planning, scheduling, reporting, or other complex B2B SaaS products.

- 
Experience working with distributed or microservice systems, a basic understanding of infrastructure and infrastructure as code, and some experience creating, improving, or debugging CI/CD pipelines.

This Role Is NOT 

- 
A ticket-taker role. If you want fully specced work handed to you, this isn't the right fit.

- 
A pixel-pusher translating finished designs into code with no say in the problem or the solution.

- 
A role where you hand off at the API boundary. If "that's a backend ticket" is your instinct, this will frustrate you.

- 
A role where quality is someone else's job. Toggl doesn't have a dedicated QA
team or layer: there's no separate team that will catch your bugs, write your
tests, or own your performance regressions.

- 
A place to work in isolation from users. You'll be expected to know who you're building for and why.

- 
A role for people who need heavy process, frequent approvals, or top-down direction to do their best work.

The Team 

We are a global team of ~80 awesome people working from over 40 countries around the globe. We hire globally, you work locally—in the heart of London, a beach outside of Río de Janeiro, or a quiet village near Florence, the choice is yours. Every few months we travel to meet up somewhere in the world and spend some quality time together. We place a huge amount of trust in our people, and we measure the outcomes rather than the work itself. Our values fuel our results.

What's Happening at Toggl 

Toggl is at an exciting turning point. We're taking our best-in-class time tracking - trusted and loved by millions of users worldwide - and expanding it into something bigger: Toggl 2.0 . One product that brings together time tracking, planning, capacity management, reporting, and insight. The idea is simple: better time tracking creates better data, which powers everything else. We call it time intelligence. We build with AI throughout, and we think it's a real multiplier for strong engineers rather than a substitute for them. The judgment, the tradeoffs, and the accountability for what ships stay with people.

Benefits 

- 
Freedom to choose when and how much you work—we only measure results

- 
24 days of paid time off a year, plus your local holidays

- 
Unlimited sick leave

- 
In-person meetups for team-building (expenses covered)

- 
4-6 weeks paid sabbatical (depending on tenure)

- 
Laptop budget up to 2,500€ and it renews every 3 years

- 
€2,000 budget to set up your home office and an additional €300 every year after 3 years of tenure

- 
€3,000 per year for co-working space membership and/or internet service at home

- 
€4,000 per year contribution to use for training, workshops, and conferences

- 
€2,400 per year contribution for any equipment or services to improve and/or maintain your physical and mental health

- 
Support for buying tools you need for doing your best work (even eyeglasses if you need a new pair)

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/toggl-senior-full-stack

title: Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations
description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.

This is a non-attorney role. You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.

As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: 

- Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1.

- Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure. 

- Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions.

- Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact.

- Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders.

Success in this role looks like: 

- In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals.

- By 6 months , you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt.

- By 12 months , you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined.

You should get in touch if: 

- Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes & investigative experience: You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care. You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record.

- You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs: You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work. 

- Strong communication skills: You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

Bonus points if: 

- 

- You have built something people actually use—an internal tool, detection model, script, automation, or AI workflow that made a manual process better. We would rather see something scrappy and useful in production than something polished in a slide.

- You have hands-on experience applying AI/ML to fraud, investigations, or compliance.

- You have a J.D., legal training, or experience working alongside Legal, SIU, or compliance at a health plan.

- You have industry certifications such as CFE, AHFI, or CHC.

Benefits Overview :

- Financial Well-Being : Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.

- Physical Well-Being : We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

- Mental Well-Being : We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 

- Professional Development : Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks: 

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities

- Reimbursement for office setup expenses

- Monthly cell phone & internet stipend

- Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams

- Paid parental leave for all new parents

- And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. title: Customer Value Architect III
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, US (Remote)

About Mixpanel 

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

About the Team 

The Customer Value Architects team sits inside the revenue organization and owns the connection between what customers buy and what they actually get out of Mixpanel. We turn product usage into measurable business outcomes, working across onboarding, adoption, and renewal to make sure customers see the value they signed up for.

About the Role 

The right candidate is a relationship-first advisor who connects a customer's Mixpanel investment to real outcomes for a defined book of accounts. You'll own the adoption and value plan for each account end to end: understanding why the customer bought Mixpanel, tracking whether they're getting the ROI they expected, and driving the enablement and product usage that gets them there. You'll build trusted relationships with business and technical stakeholders, partner closely with your Account Executive and renewal counterparts, and bring a growing point of view on how customers should think about AI in their product workflows. This role suits someone who can own a project end to end and is ready to start extending their influence beyond their own accounts to the wider team.

Responsibilities 

- Own the value plan for each account in your portfolio, connecting the business problem that led the customer to buy Mixpanel with the outcomes they measure.

- Build relationships with business and technical stakeholders, aligning Mixpanel's capabilities to what customers care about most.

- Run discovery on customer priorities and pain points, and turn what you learn into concrete adoption plans and internal updates.

- Partner with your Account Executive on expansion and your renewal counterpart on renewal execution, bringing the value case and adoption evidence that supports both.

- Lead enablement/best practices sessions on dashboard design, funnel analysis, and retention modeling to grow how deeply and widely a customer uses Mixpanel.

- Monitor usage and health signals and lead business reviews that surface what's working, deepen adoption, and catch risk early.

- Spot underused features and contracted capabilities, and turn them into clear recommendations for the customer.

- Triage product questions and issues, solving what you can and routing the rest to the right team.

- Build a working point of view on a customer's AI maturity, and use Mixpanel's own AI surface to help them build on their product data.

- Coordinate with GTM, Product, and Engineering on escalations, and share what works with the broader Customer Value Architects team.

We're Looking For Someone Who Has 

- 4 - 6 years of experience in customer success, consulting, or a related field supporting B2B SaaS accounts, or equivalent experience.

- A track record of managing relationships across a range of stakeholders, from business partners to technical teams.

- The ability to translate technical concepts, like data models and product metrics, into terms that land with non-technical stakeholders.

- Experience turning product usage into a clear story about customer outcomes and ROI.

- Comfort building and running adoption plans that tie daily work to a customer's larger goals.

- Hands-on experience with AI or agentic tooling beyond casual use, such as MCP-based workflows or LLM copilots.

- A collaborative approach to working across account teams and internal partners to move plans forward.

- Good judgment for prioritizing which accounts and actions need attention first.

Bonus Points For 

- Background in product analytics, growth, or data-driven product development.

- Experience in a technical advisory or professional services capacity.

- Familiarity with analytics instrumentation, event tracking, or data tooling.

title: Head of Technology
description:
Headquarters: New York City

URL: https://sanctuary.computer 

We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.

Original job posting link 

About garden3d 

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development 

At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design 

When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Index - Community 

Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.

We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.

garden3d TK — Media 

At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone 
Mill 
IngredientAI 

⛰️ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates 

️ Systems that hold up 

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development 

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering 

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer 

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best 

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery 

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business 

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense 

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story 

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture 

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

Special Projects 

In addition to day to day responsibilities, here’s an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years →

- Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts

- Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from

- Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do

- Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio

- Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products

- Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed

Qualifications

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:

Must have: 

- 12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company

- Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products

- A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native

- A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure

- All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase

- Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it

- Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients

- A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them

- Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)

Nice-to-have: 

- A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products

- Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)

- Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role

- Open source projects they've started or maintained

- Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams

- Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company

- A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring

- Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality

Who you are

The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart” by carefully managing their workflow and team.

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

Compensation

This is a permanent leadership role. If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.

We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $110 - $175 p/hr pending seniori

About the Role: 

Maven is looking for a Director of Marketing Operations who will own the systems, data, and reporting infrastructure behind our B2B Growth Marketing team — from HubSpot/Salesforce instrumentation to pipeline attribution to the budget that funds it all. This person will lead a team across marketing analytics, marketing operations, and web optimization, and serve as the go-to partner for Sales, RevOps, Strategic Finance, and Client Success on shared data and reporting. Reporting to the Senior Director of Growth, they'll bring structure and rigor to a fast-moving org, ensuring marketing's numbers hold up in front of executive leadership.

What You’ll Do: 

Marketing Technology, Data & Attribution

- HubSpot instrumentation (and its integration with Salesforce): own lead management strategy, campaign orchestration and tracking, and stage definitions for the B2B funnel.

- Pipeline attribution: own marketing's multi-touch attribution methodology and represent it in cross-team pipeline conversations.

- Data governance: maintain data dictionaries and definitions (MQL/MQA thresholds, pipeline vs. bookings vs. revenue) so reporting stays consistent as tools and AI use expand.

- Martech stack: own B2B-facing tools and integrations, including CaliberMind, GA4, HubSpot, Qualified, Webflow, and evaluate new tooling as needs evolve.

- Training and enablement: ensure the has the resources and knowledge to own the reporting and orchestration of their channels.

Analytics & Reporting

- KPI ownership: define and maintain B2B marketing metrics (MQLs, MQAs, pipeline coverage, Pipe-Spend ratio) and the reporting cadence behind them.

- Executive reporting: build and deliver pipeline briefings and performance readouts for B2B marketing leadership.

- Dashboards: own the B2B analytics stack across CaliberMind, Looker, Data Studio, Salesforce, and GA4, and keep it accurate as definitions change.

- FY planning support: partner with Strategic Finance and RevOps on fiscal year target-setting, run-rate projections, and scenario modeling for B2B pipeline and budget as well as org-level OKR setting.

Budget & Planning

- Budget ownership: oversee the B2B marketing budget, including forecast, actuals, monthly reconciliation, and shifts across programs and months.

- Vendor management: track spend and manage relationships with external vendors.

- FY planning: lead annual and quarterly budgeting and planning for B2B Growth Marketing in partnership with Strategic Finance.

Marketing Website & CRO

- Marketing website: manage the web team that owns navigation, landing pages, and on-page SEO/AEO for the Enterprise/B2B experience.

- Testing and optimization: run a structured A/B testing and CRO program for B2B landing pages.

- Accessibility: maintain WCAG 2.1 AA compliance across the B2B site experience.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership

- 

- People leadership: manage and develop a team covering marketing analytics, marketing operations, and web optimization.

- Process and tooling: set the team's operating rhythm and own its project management tooling (Asana and Jira).

- Builds with AI: personally build AI-powered workflows for reporting, analysis, and campaign operations that enable the team to make better decisions and scale without additional headcount.

- AI enablement: lead rollout of AI tools within B2B Growth Marketing, including data governance for tools connected to live CRM and marketing data, and set the team's judgment for where AI helps and where it doesn't.

- Cross-functional partnership: serve as B2B Growth Marketing's primary point of contact for Sales, SDR, RevOps, Strategic Finance, and Client Success on shared data, process, and reporting questions.

What You’ll Bring: 

- 8+ years in B2B marketing operations, analytics, or revenue operations, ideally supporting complex or enterprise sales cycles.

- Hands-on ownership of a marketing automation platform (HubSpot or similar) and the integration with Salesforce, including lead routing, lifecycle stages, and campaign orchestration.

- Experience building and defending pipeline or marketing attribution models with Sales and Finance stakeholders.

- Track record owning multi-million dollar marketing budgets, including forecasting, actuals, and reconciliation.

- Experience owning a B2B marketing website and CRO program, including A/B testing and accessibility standards.

- Experience managing and developing a high performance team.

- Sharp, direct communicator, comfortable presenting pipeline and Marketing performance data to executive leadership.

- Comfortable operating in a fast-changing org structure and building processes from ambiguity.

- Experience rolling out AI tools within a marketing team, with an eye toward data governance and accuracy.

The base salary range for this role is $170,000 - $200,000 per year. You will also be entitled to receive equity and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, and skillset.

Maven is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer. About the Role: 

We are looking for a mission-driven health coach to join our team to provide world-class care delivery services to Maven members. Our Care Delivery team consists of care coaches and care advocates who help our members navigate digital care and access the tools to unlock their best experience and outcomes. Our team works to continuously learn more about members and ourselves, and you’ll move fast to adapt and grow as we implement data-driven strategies for improving the lives of our members through a shared coaching model. As a Care Coach, you’ll coordinate care for our members beyond the digital space. Through goal setting and program opt-in, you’ll drive behavior change and improved outcomes for higher risk members. 

Our Care Delivery team works remotely and supports Maven members 24/7/365. We are currently hiring for the following shift:

- Monday-Friday 3-11:30p EST

What You’ll Do: 

- Drive program engagement by clearly communicating the value of Maven’s care coaching model, optimizing opt-in rates, and supporting long-term behavior change

- Co-create SMART goals with members and own their progress by tracking adherence, adjusting care plans, and course-correcting within Maven’s clinical program design

- Manage a caseload of members and engage with them through ongoing messaging, video appointments, and outreach

- Adhere to clinical program guidelines and protocols while utilizing motivational interviewing skills and behavior modification techniques to remove barriers, influence sustained behavior change, and promote optimal health outcomes for members

- Move fast to assess member knowledge and barriers and provide personalized health education to members across varying ages, backgrounds, cultures, and literacy levels

- Collaborate with providers on members’ care teams to translate clinical recommendations into actionable next steps

- Lead with data by remotely monitoring member health data and platform activity to identify risks early and follow established protocols and procedures to take appropriate action

- Remove barriers to care by coordinating seamlessly across Maven’s digital network, in-person provider networks, and external partners as needed

- Embrace a continuous-learning mindset by participating in and leading efforts to improve quality of care and clinical outcomes

- Act as a team player by providing coverage to ensure that all members across the Maven platform receive appropriate care and timely responses when needed

What You’ll Bring: 

- 1- 2+ years experience in clinical work as a nurse (RN) with focus on patient education, motivational interviewing, and driving clinical outcomes

- Demonstrated experience working with the maternity population and/or individuals navigating family planning or fertility care (trying to conceive, undergoing fertility treatment)

- Training and experience coaching individuals to achieve specific health outcomes (ie, medication management, nutrition and exercise goals, managing blood pressure)

- Ability to remain flexible with changes, work efficiently to meet member demand and have a growth mindset

- Ability to communicate with patients empathetically in writing and verbally, and passionate about creating a positive member experience with optimal outcomes 

- Experience achieving KPIs relevant to patient outcomes, including but not limited to opt-in rates, follow-up adherence and member satisfaction 

- Demonstrated ability to quickly learn and adapt to new digital health tools and platforms, with comfort operating in a fast-changing tech environment

- Embrace AI tools as part of daily workflows to enhance efficiency and improve member outcomes

- Strong telehealth competency, including comfort in conducting phone outreach and video calls. Reliable access to high-speed internet

- Health coaching certification (NBC-HWC or ICF) is preferred, not required 

- Experience in a start-up or fast-paced environment with ability to navigate systems quickly and adapt to change is preferred, not required 

- Experience coaching across multiple modalities such as video, text/chat, and phone; adapting communication style to fit member need is preferred, not required 

- Comfort with technology tools like Google suite, CRM platforms, EHRs, and Zendesk is preferred, not required 

The base salary range for this role is $62,000 - $78,000 per year. You will also be entitled to receive equity and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, and skillset.

This role requires active work authorization in the US. 

Maven embraces a flexible and inclusive work environment. This role is open to candidate in: AZ, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, KS, MA, MD, ME, MI, MN, MO, NC, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, VA, VT, WI. Maven is committed to supporting remote team members with the tools and collaborative culture needed to thrive regardless of location. description:
